item.content:encoded:
I like it overall. Good atmosphere, brief and logical containment procedures, a sensical description of the pathology of the organism and its host, etc. However, this sentence: "An ingenious method exists of using the host’s own digestive system to process pieces of organic materials collected by the warriors into a nutritive slurry that feeds both the colony and sustains the host hive structure.", bothers me. They're non-sapien insects. It's not like some really smart moth in the colony said "I think we should use the host's digestive system to process organic matter into nutritive slurry". It's a biological process and ascribing human-like qualities really detracts from the clinical tone.

Then again this is a series one. The formula for SCP writing wasn't quite as standardized back then.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
NOPE NOPE NOPE. +1

I love this SCP. This article is what originally drew me into the site. I think the slight background, the wording, everything is just about perfect. Even the 'unprofessional' use of "Incredibly" and "ingenious" actually make it seem more real to me, because scientists AREN'T technical writers and often let their emotions slip into their reports. This is clearly a cold, eccentric scientist writing a report about an organism he finds biologically fascinating. Hes's so engrossed, he obviously doesn't have any qualms about purposefully testing this thing on live humans, D-Class or not. Then the last paragraph… the horror of what is happening finally dawns on him and manages to convince even HIM, Mr. Cold Mad Scientist, that this… horror… goes too far.

To anyone complaining that it's too mundane, that it's not anomalous enough… well, that just adds to the creepiness, doesn't it? That just adds something to the idea that maybe, just maybe, these things might really exist and are gonna get you while you sleep.

The ONE thing I would change about this article has been mentioned already: the Hive should create something like 2-5 new Queens, not just one to replace the original. It can't be too many or we would wonder why we haven't heard about it in the news, but with just one we wonder how it managed to survive this long, and hey, its obviously the only one AND its contained so odds are its not going to find us. Adding a slight hint that there might be a few more out there would make things a touch scarier in my opinion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I finished reading the article.

I rolled my eyes up in my head.

I made a low hissing sound.

I do not know why. I think it was just the reaction my brain picked to express "Holy shiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiit creepyyyyyyyyyy."

But yeah, about the only issue I have with it is the thing about the colony producing one replacement queen and then going splodey. Unless the implication is supposed to be that both queens are still viable after the splodey, in which case that probably works fine. Though it seems a terribly inefficient sort of insect that goes to all that time and effort to only produce a single progeny. My personal suggestion would be to change it so that it produces a fairly large number of potential Queens, but most die in the explosion. The living ones are then carried off by the Workers, and the ones strong enough to survive eventually devour the Workers before becoming capable of going out and seeking prey. That would keep the produced numbers low but still keep it in the range of these things being viable and surviving all this time.

But A) it's an SCP's prerogative to not make good biological sense and B) as everyone says it's achieved a ton of votes just as it is, so that's just my personal thoughts and no particular urgings or demanding to change it. That's usually my thought process on commenting anyway.
